title: Personal Project Ideas: Sport Topics for MYP
summary: Personal Project ideas sport students can use, with 10 practical topics, learning and product goals, success criteria, and a complete MYP example.
body_markdown:
A love of sport is a useful starting point for the MYP Personal Project, but “football” is an interest, not yet a project. Learning how training design affects passing accuracy, then creating and testing a programme, gives that interest a direction.


If you searched for **Personal Project ideas sport** , start here: choose something you want to learn, create a product that demonstrates that learning, and keep it manageable enough to test. The project includes a process, a product or outcome, and a reflective report, with approaches to learning skills assessed throughout. RevisionDojo’s guide to[what the MYP Personal Project involves](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-is-the-myp-personal-project) explains the foundations.


### A quick project checklist


Before committing, ask:


- What knowledge or skill will I learn?
- What product or outcome will I create?
- Can I complete and test it with available resources?
- Who could provide useful feedback?
- What evidence will demonstrate progress?
- How will I evaluate the product?


Athletic ability is not a prerequisite. Sport projects can explore coaching, psychology, design, nutrition, accessibility, history, or data analysis.


### 10 Personal Project ideas for sport


Project idea Learning goal Product goal


Football passing programme Understand practice structure, technique, and feedback. Create and test a 4-week programme with progress records.


Beginner running guide Understand pacing, recovery, and gradual progression. Produce a beginner schedule reviewed for safety and practicality.


Sports psychology podcast Explore concentration, confidence, and preparation routines. Record a short series explaining mental preparation techniques.


Inclusive PE activity pack Learn to adapt rules, equipment, and communication. Create and trial activities for different physical needs.


Basketball shooting analysis Investigate technique and shooting consistency. Produce a video analysis and personalised drill plan.


Sustainable sportswear prototype Explore fabric properties and environmental considerations. Make a sports accessory using carefully selected materials.


Athlete nutrition recipe book Research balanced nutrition and individual needs. Create recipes reviewed by an appropriate expert.


Local sport history exhibition Investigate community history and source reliability. Build an exhibition using interviews and credited sources.


Match statistics dashboard Learn to analyse sporting data and its limitations. Build a spreadsheet or coded visual dashboard.


Coaching tutorial series Explore demonstrations, feedback, and suitable instructions. Film beginner tutorials and revise after viewer feedback.


Adapt the sport, audience, timescale, or format to your circumstances. These[realistic Personal Project examples](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/real-examples-of-ib-myp-personal-projects-for-inspiration) show how broad interests become manageable projects.

### Turning one idea into a full Personal Project


Imagine your football passing becomes less accurate when you move quickly. Before collecting drills, identify what you need to understand and how you could evaluate your design.


### Define the learning and product goals


A focused learning goal might be:


> I will learn how passing technique, movement, practice structure, and feedback can support short-range football passing accuracy.


This describes the learning. The corresponding product goal identifies what you will create:


> I will design, complete, and evaluate a 4-week football passing programme containing eight drill sessions, technique guidance, baseline and final tests, and a progress tracker.


The goals support each other without repeating the same statement. Neither promises exceptional athletic performance. RevisionDojo’s guide to[writing a strong MYP Personal Project goal](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/strong-myp-personal-project-goal) explores this distinction.


### Create measurable success criteria


Words such as “professional” or “interesting” need clearer definitions before they become useful criteria. Your programme could instead be required to:


- contain eight sessions across four weeks;
- include instructions, equipment, timings, and safety notes;
- address stationary and moving passes;
- use the same defined test before and after training;
- receive feedback from a coach or PE teacher;
- include revisions based on testing and feedback.


These criteria evaluate the product without promising improvement. Choose standards that fit your resources and explain how you will judge each one. The[MYP Personal Project criteria guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-personal-project-criteria) connects planning, skill application, and reflection.


### Plan evidence before beginning


Useful evidence includes dated plans, source evaluations, unsuccessful trials, feedback, test results, and explanations of changes. Keep passing records, annotate technique videos, and explain why you modified particular drills.


Set consistent testing conditions where practical, including distance, target size, and number of attempts. Obtain appropriate consent before recording others, protect their privacy, and follow school guidance on physical activity.


Organise your timeline around research, baseline testing, prototype drills, feedback, completion, and evaluation. Reviewing[common Personal Project mistakes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/common-myp-personal-project-mistakes-e0513f75) can help you spot missing steps before work begins.


### Reflect on decisions


“I completed my drills” records an event. Reflection explains what the result suggested, which skills you applied, and why your next decision changed.


Improvement would not prove that one drill caused it. Motivation, fatigue, or familiarity with the test could also influence results. Acknowledge those limits and evaluate the product against your criteria, even when the outcome differs from your hopes.

### Build a project you can explain


Choose a question you care about, a product you can test, and evidence that makes your decisions visible. Expensive equipment and dramatic performance gains are unnecessary. What matters is showing how research shaped your work and what evaluation taught you.
